subject: Temporary exception request: overnight P2 response window - Nimbus Retail
messages:
From: Keenan Marsh <kmarsh@nimbusretail.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary overnight P2 response modification

Hi Diego,

We’ve been tracking overnight usage for our Redwood-backed inference endpoints and traffic drops to ~3% of daily volume between 02:00-06:00 PT. Given that, our on-call costs and rotations are disproportionate to the risk. We’d like to request a temporary modification to our support response commitments for P2 incidents during that overnight window:

- Current commitment: P2 response within 1 hour (24/7)
- Requested temporary change: P2 response within 3 hours between 02:00–06:00 PT
- Duration: 90 days starting 2026-10-01 (we can extend if metrics support it)

We’re happy to accept stricter monitoring, automatic failover routing (if available), and a weekly health check from Redwood. In return, we’d like a proportional service credit if P2s occur outside agreed fallback policies.

Attached: usage-report-q3.csv (hourly volumes).

Can you confirm whether this exception path is possible and what the operational controls would look like?

Thanks,
Keenan Marsh
Director of Platform Operations
Nimbus Retail

--
Attachment: usage-report-q3.csv (CSV summary, 120KB)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Keenan Marsh <kmarsh@nimbusretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary overnight P2 response modification

Keenan —

Thanks for the clear background and the Q3 usage data. I appreciate the pragmatic ask. I’m looping in Marissa (Customer Success lead) and Ben (Support manager) to scope the operational impact and draft a short mutual action plan.

High level thought: a temporary, documented SLA carveout is doable, provided we:
- Capture an exception form for legal/compliance review
- Define fallback routing and automated alerts (so we don’t miss regressions)
- Agree on credits or remediation if coverage fails

Marissa/Ben — can you propose an ops plan and a list of required artifacts (SLA exception form, runbook edits, monitoring thresholds)? Keenan — I suggest a quick 30-min sync if helpful; otherwise we’ll send the plan for signoff.

Proposed target start: 2026-10-01 (to give ops 2 weeks to land changes).

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

--
(Inline: forwarding usage-report-q3.csv)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Keenan Marsh <kmarsh@nimbusretail.com>, Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Operational proposal for Nimbus overnight P2 carveout

Diego / Ben / Keenan —

Thanks for looping me in. I’ve discussed with Support Ops and SRE; below is a proposal that balances lower overnight traffic with acceptable risk controls.

Proposal (90-day trial, 2026-10-01 -> 2026-12-30):

1) Coverage window adjustment
   - P2 response window between 02:00–06:00 PT will be 3 hours (acknowledge + initial triage). P1 remains 1-hour 24/7.

2) Twilight responder and automatic escalation
   - We will assign a ‘twilight’ shift (covering 23:00–03:00 PT) and configure automatic escalation to a regional on-call in case a P2 is not acknowledged within 60 minutes. If acknowledgment fails, regional fallback triggers and on-call paging continues.

3) Monitoring & health checks
   - We’ll enable synthetic checks on your critical endpoints (5m cadence) and a weekly status digest. Any increase >30% in late-night error rate will automatically pause the carveout and revert to full 1-hour P2 coverage until reviewed.

4) Remediation & credits
   - If an eligible P2 is missed due to coverage lapse during the carveout window and fallback did not execute, we propose a one-time 15% credit against the monthly service invoice for the month in which the miss occurred. (Financial to confirm).

5) Required artifacts
   - Complete SLA_exception_request_form.pdf (attached)
   - Signed DocuSign amendment (I’ll generate link)
   - Updated runbook and support-rotation-proposal.xlsx

Next steps:
- Keenan: sign and return SLA_exception_request_form.pdf to contracts@nimbusretail.com and confirm acceptance of the proposed credit approach.
- Ben/Support Ops: I’ll attach the rotation spreadsheet and preliminary runbook updates.
- Diego: I’ll prepare DocuSign amendment and copy Stephanie in billing for credit approval.

Attaching: SLA_exception_request_form.pdf, support-rotation-proposal.xlsx

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: SLA_exception_request_form.pdf, support-rotation-proposal.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>, Keenan Marsh <kmarsh@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational proposal for Nimbus overnight P2 carveout

Marissa — thanks, this looks sensible operationally. A few clarifications from Support/Billing perspective:

- Credit mechanics: Stephanie, is 15% a plausible one-off credit for a verified coverage-miss month? We need a billing code and an approver flow.
- KPI to unpause carveout: please confirm the concrete metric (I suggest 0.5% increase in 5xx rate or sustained >20% rise in error budget consumption over 3 days).
- Shift staffing: twilight shift will be pulled from the regional pool; we estimate +0.2 FTE for the trial window.

Keenan — can you confirm that Nimbus is comfortable with an automatic pause condition if the synthetic checks breach the threshold? That’s the main safety valve to prevent regressions.

Ben Carter
Manager, Support Operations
Redwood Inference

--
(Reference: internal runbook excerpt attached to ticket)

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 08:20:00 -0700
Subject: Final: proposed SLA amendment & next steps (action required)

Keenan / Olivia —

Appreciate the quick collaboration. Below is the final operational summary and the immediate next steps to put the temporary carveout into effect on 2026-10-01.

Summary (agreed):
- Window: 02:00–06:00 PT, P2 response = 3 hours (ack + triage). P1 unchanged.
- Duration: 90 days (2026-10-01 through 2026-12-30).
- Safeguards: synthetic checks (5m cadence); automatic pause on metric breach; twilight shift + regional fallback routing.
- Credits: one-time 15% credit for a verified coverage miss month (to be finalized by billing).

Next steps / action items:
1) Keenan: please review and sign the SLA_exception_request_form.pdf and the DocuSign amendment. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/tx/ABCD-2026-NR-SLA (attached as docusign-sla-amendment-link.txt).
2) Keenan: confirm acceptance of the 15% credit approach or propose alternate remediation by 2026-09-22.
3) Marissa/Ben: finalize runbook updates and configure synthetic monitors by 2026-09-28.
4) Stephanie: confirm billing code and approval workflow for credits.

If we don’t hear back from Nimbus by end of next week we’ll schedule a 20-minute call to review. Once signed we’ll apply changes on 2026-10-01.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this in place smoothly.

Diego Fernandez
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
